landscape.label: Why Window Film Here
landscape.title: Why Window Film Makes Sense in Philadelphia's Climate
landscape.say: Philadelphia gets both ends of the weather. July and August bring sticky, humid heat, with afternoons that sit in the 90s and nights that barely cool off. Then January turns raw and grey, with wind coming down the long straight streets of the grid.

landscape.say: For homes: Home Tinting: General home window tinting for Philly houses and condos, picked by which way each window faces and what the room is used for, from a sunny front parlor to a top-floor bedroom. Heat Control: Film that rejects a share of summer solar heat on south and west glass, so rooms in rowhomes, twins and glassy new builds stay closer to the temperature you set. UV Protection: Clear film that screens out almost all ultraviolet rays, so hardwood, rugs, art and upholstery in sun-struck rooms keep their color for longer. Privacy: Frosted, gradient and daytime one-way films for street-level rowhome windows, bathrooms and side windows that face a neighbor a few feet away.

landscape.say: For businesses: Storefront: Clear UV and heat film for retail glass on Philly shopping corridors, keeping displays visible while slowing fading and cutting afternoon heat in the shop. Commercial Security: Shatter-resistant film for storefronts, offices, clinics and schools, often paired with attachment systems that anchor the film to the window frame. Anti-Graffiti: Replaceable clear film that takes the scratches, acid etching and marker tags instead of the glass, so damaged storefront panes do not need replacing. Decorative & Frosted Glass: Frosted, etched-look and printed films for glass partitions, entry doors and lobbies, including logos and bands at eye level on office glass.

landscape.label: Local Know-How
landscape.title: Window Film for Philadelphia Rowhomes, Twins and Stone Houses
landscape.say: The city's housing stock shapes what film people ask for. In a typical rowhouse in South Philly, Point Breeze or Brewerytown, the front window sits right on the sidewalk, so anyone walking by can see straight into the living room. Privacy film and daytime one-way films are the most common requests on these blocks, along with a little extra security for basement and rear windows facing an alley.

landscape.label: How It Works
landscape.title: How an install works

tiles.s: Start with the address, a rough count of windows
Film needs time to dry fully

landscape.say: Here's how an install works. First, start with the address, a rough count of windows, which way they face and the problem you have in mind. Then, they confirm the glass type, look at frame and seal condition and note any historic district or condo association concerns. On install day, they clean the glass thoroughly, cut film to each pane and squeegee out the water and air. Finally, film needs time to dry fully, and cold Philadelphia winters slow that down.
